 Hridoy, Das lead Bangladesh fightback after Rabada five-for
 Towhid Hridoy's century and Litton Das' unbeaten 92 helped Bangladesh recover to 327/6 after Kagiso Rabada's five-wicket haul.
 15 November, 2026 SOUTH AFRICA v BANGLADESH, 1st TEST, SCORECARD 
 Towhid Hridoy and Litton Das led a spirited Bangladesh fightback on the opening day of the first ICC World Test Championship contest against South Africa in Johannesburg, overcoming an early Kagiso Rabada onslaught to put the visitors in a promising position at stumps.
 View this post on Instagram 
 Towhid continued his good recent form as he stroked an impressive 137, while Das was unbeaten on 92* at stumps as Bangladesh reached 327/6 after they were 22/3 earlier in the day.
 Opener Tanzid Hasan also contributed a solid 67 and the left-hander is hoping Bangladesh can keep piling on the runs on Monday when play resumes.
 "We had two very good partnerships today. After losing early wickets, we managed to build a partnership, and then Litton Das and Towhid Hridoy put together an outstanding 200-run stand. It was truly exceptional," Tanzid said at stumps.
 "The longer we can bat tomorrow morning, the better it will be for us. Runs will come naturally if we spend more time at the crease. So, I believe batting for as long as possible is the best approach."
 Rabada was easily the pick of the South Africa bowlers as he contributed figures of 5/51 on the opening day, though the pace spearhead felt his side missed a big opportunity to dismiss Bangladesh cheaply.
 "Perhaps we just let them off the hook here and there and didn't string together enough dots or enough wicket-taking balls, especially with the old ball. I wouldn't say we're absolutely happy with that. But we're just in the position that we are in right now and we've got to fight."
 View this post on Instagram 
 After Bangladesh opted to bat, Rabada wasted little time making an impact, striking with the very first delivery of the Test series to dismiss Mahfijul Islam.
 The South African pacer continued his early onslaught, sending Mominul Haque back to the pavilion in his next over before bowling Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto with a beauty to claim his third wicket of the innings.
 Bangladesh found some much-needed stability through Tanzid and Towhid, who stitched together a 99-run partnership to revive the innings.
 However, Rabada returned to break the stand, dismissing Hasan, who had looked well set on 67. 
 The Proteas quick struck again off the very next delivery, removing Mushfiqur Rahim to complete his 18th five-wicket haul in Test cricket and leave Bangladesh reeling at 121/5.
 With half the side back in the pavilion, Das joined Hridoy in the middle, and the pair produced a remarkable fightback to turn the innings around.
 Hridoy continued his impressive run of form, bringing up his second Test century in as many matches after his memorable double century against the West Indies earlier this month. 
 The right-hander eventually fell for a magnificent 137, with Marco Jansen producing a superb delivery to trap him leg-before and end a mammoth 206-run partnership.
 The pair's superb 206-run stand for the sixth wicket is the highest stand for any wicket for Bangladesh against South Africa.
 Das, meanwhile, remained unbeaten on 92, guiding Bangladesh to 327/6 at stumps after a resilient batting display that helped the visitors recover from a precarious position.
 Series schedule
 First Test: 15-19 November, Johannesburg
 Second Test : 23-27 November, Centurion
